        self.assertEqual(result, 3)

import re
from collections import Counter

def word_count(text):
    words = re.split(r'\W+', text)
    return len(words)

def top_words(text, n):
    words = re.split(r'\W+', text)
    counts = Counter(words)
    return counts.most_common(n)

The issue is clear: the regex `r'\W+'` splits on all non-word characters, which includes apostrophes. This causes "don't" to become ["don", "t"] instead of ["don't"]. Also, the word_count includes empty strings from split. For the ties test, apostrophes are being removed, so the sorting isn't working. Let me fix both functions:
